claims.claim: young banded killifish in Lake Opinicon grow linearly to 49.5 mm by mid-October (Keast & Eadie 1984 via COSEWIC 2014)
claims.note: COSEWIC 2014 (printed p. 10, PDF p. 20) says young-of-year 'reach a mean length of 49.5 mm by the middle of October', citing Keast and Eadie 1984 — so the via citation is faithful to COSEWIC. But the Keast & Eadie abstract says length gains were linear early in summer, 'reached a plateau by early September' and few species grew beyond September, and the methods summary lists the last collections as 'early September and early October' — 'linear to mid-October' may be COSEWIC's paraphrase. Needs the article's table for killifish

claims.claim: first-summer length grows roughly linearly through early summer and plateaus by early September, and spawning date is the strongest influence on autumn size (abstract, nine species in Lake Opinicon)
claims.note: the abstract says exactly this ('length increments were linear early in the summer and reached a plateau by early September'; 'Spawning date had the greatest influence on the amount of growth attained'); unchecked under rule 1 (abstract only). The paper already marks it 'abstract'

notes: Study: Lake Opinicon, Ontario (2,200 ha, eutrophic), 1977; inshore shallows and weed beds seined weekly from late June to the third week of August, plus early September and early October; 7 × 2 m bag seine, 0.15-cm mesh; 60–80 fish per species per collection; total lengths. Abstract: species grew 6–10-fold in length; early spawners ended larger; small-bodied species had the longest spawning seasons and the widest size range by summer's end; no link between diet type and growth. The 49.5 mm rests on COSEWIC 2014 (wildlife-species.canada.ca, 'sr_Banded Killifish_2014_e.pdf'); if the article cannot be had, cite COSEWIC 2014 for it and say 'by October' rather than 'by mid-October'.
